content:
Let the arithmetic sequence have first term \(a_1=4\) and common difference \(d\).
Since every term is an integer, \(a_2=4+d\) is an integer, so \(d\) must be an integer.

Because the sequence contains both \(24\) and \(34\), there are positive integers \(m,n\) such that  
\[
4+(m-1)d=24 \qquad\text{and}\qquad 4+(n-1)d=34.
\]
Hence
\[
(m-1)d=20 \quad\text{and}\quad (n-1)d=30.
\]
So \(d\) must divide both \(20\) and \(30\), i.e. \(d\mid \gcd(20,30)=10\).

Since the sequence starts at \(4\) and must later reach \(24\) and \(34\), the common difference must be positive.  
Thus the possible values of \(d\) are the positive divisors of \(10\):
\[
d=1,\; 2,\; 5,\; 10.
\]

For each such sequence, the \(10\)th term is
\[
a_{10}=4+9d.
\]

Now compute the sum of all these \(10\)th terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d\mid 10,\; d>0} (4+9d)
&= (4+9\cdot1)+(4+9\cdot2)+(4+9\cdot5)+(4+9\cdot10) \\
&= 13+22+49+94 \\
&= 178.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{178}
\]
